title: Blood
lead: In the Bible blood is life. It may not be eaten (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:10–14), it is given on the altar to make atonement (Leviticus 17:11), it seals the covenant (Exodus 24:8), and the New Testament sees all of this fulfilled in the blood of Christ (Hebrews 9:11–22).

sections.b: Abel's blood cries from the ground (Genesis 4:10), and after the flood God forbids eating blood and spilling human blood (Genesis 9:4–6). The Passover blood on the doorposts protects Israel (Exodus 12:13), and Moses splashes "the blood of the covenant" on the people at Sinai (Exodus 24:8). Leviticus explains why: "a body's life is in its blood," given by God on the altar to make atonement (Leviticus 17:11). Jesus at the Last Supper calls the cup "my blood of the covenant" (Mark 14:24). Hebrews argues that his blood achieves what animal blood pointed to (Hebrews 9:11–22), and the Jerusalem council asks Gentile believers to avoid eating blood (Acts 15:20, 29).
